proof:
# Exact budget-preserving descent from a product of identical simplices

This is a bounded test of second-order and projective mechanisms, not a
general extremal classification or an OC proof.

Let P be a finite set with more than one point in its affine span E,
let its arithmetic mean be p_0 in P, and let K be a d-simplex centered
at its centroid 0, d>=1. Translate the base so p_0=0. Put S=P times K,
M=|P||K| and Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d. Suppose its maximum normalized ambient
depth is Gamma. This hypothesis, for example, follows for centrally
symmetric P from the independently proved paired-centroid-tail theorem
and its symmetric-noise corollary. It is not asserted for every P.

Then the product is not a local minimum on its positive projective base
orbit. If d>=2, it is not a local minimum even among actual positive
families on the SAME fixed base P. Both assertions have exact finite
cap covers and require no differentiability of a maximizing center.

## 1. The only deepest point and a strict gap at other bases

Let lambda_0,...,lambda_d be the simplex barycentric affine functions,
and write lambda_j(x)=1/(d+1)+l_j(x), where the l_j are linear and
sum_j l_j=0. At any point (p,x), the horizontal ambient halfspaces
give its mixed depth at most its ordinary depth in K. The simplex
has maximum Gamma only at x=0: away from 0 some lambda_j(x)>1/(d+1),
and its vertex cap has fraction (1-lambda_j(x))^d<Gamma.

At (p,0) with p!=0, take one horizontal vertex cap l_j(x)>=0 and
perturb it to

    l_j(x)+t a.(q-p)>=0

with a.p>0. The cut is strictly proper in every fiber for small t.
If alpha=d/(d+1), its raw mass is exactly

    |K| sum_(q in P) [alpha+t a.(q-p)]^d.

Its derivative at zero is
-d alpha^(d-1)|K||P| a.p<0, because sum q=0. Thus this cap has mass
less than Gamma M for small positive t. It follows that (p,0) also
has depth less than Gamma. The hypothesized maximum Gamma is therefore
attained only at (0,0).

The restricted maximum at every other base is strictly below Gamma,
by the continuity of depth on each compact fiber. The exact critical-cap
construction supplies a finite whole-fiber circuit cover at each such
base with all cap masses strictly below Q=Gamma M. Keep those covers
fixed. They retain that strict slack under either of the continuous
positive-fiber or density perturbations used below.

## 2. Fixed-base affine-radius descent when d>=2

Choose a nonzero linear A on E which is nonzero at some point of P.
For sufficiently small signed t put

    r_p(t)=1+t A(p)>0,       K_p(t)=r_p(t)K.

These are actual compatible sections on the ORIGINAL P. Indeed their
support functions are r_p(t)h_K(u), affine in p for each u. More directly,
for any anchored representation p=sum alpha_q q, the Minkowski sum
sum alpha_q r_q(t)K equals r_p(t)K exactly.

For j=0,...,d use the ambient cap

    H_j(t)={ (p,x): l_j(x)-t alpha A(p)>=0 }.          (1)

They cover the ENTIRE fiber plane above 0, since A(0)=0 and sum l_j=0.
In fiber p, writing x=r_p(t)X with X in K, their threshold is

    lambda_j(X)>=1/(d+1)+t alpha A(p)/r_p(t).

For small t all these thresholds are in (0,1). The raw cap volume is

    |K| r_p(t)^d
       [alpha-t alpha A(p)/r_p(t)]^d
       =Gamma |K|.                                    (2)

Thus every cap (1) has EXACT constant total mass Q. Meanwhile

    M(t)=|K| sum_p [1+t A(p)]^d > |P||K|=M            (3)

for every sufficiently small nonzero t when d>=2. This is strict Jensen
for the strictly convex function s^d on positive s, using sum A(p)=0
and the fact that the values are not all equal.

Together with the fixed slack covers from Section 1, the caps (1)
cover every new candidate fiber plane. Their masses are at most Q,
with strict slack for the fixed nondeep groups. Hence

    maxdepth(S(t))<=Q/M(t)<Gamma.

This is an actual fixed-base descent even though all original anchored
compatibility equalities are active. It is not an arbitrary nonlinear
map asserted to preserve the lattice: only the continuous fiber radii
change, and their compatibility was checked exactly.

## 3. Projective orbit descent for every d>=1

Keep the original fibers fixed and give their original volume densities
the exact weights [1+t A(p)]^(-d). As in the projective-orbit note, this
is the pullback of unweighted volume on the actual family obtained by

    (p,x)->(p/[1+t A(p)], x/[1+t A(p)]).

Its changed finite base has the same convex traces and the same Helly
number. It is not claimed to be the original integer lattice.

Use instead the original-coordinate cap

    J_j(t)={ (p,x):l_j(x)+t alpha A(p)>=0 }.           (4)

Again they cover the whole plane at base 0. Its weighted cap volume
in fiber p is

    |K| [1+t A(p)]^(-d)[alpha+t alpha A(p)]^d
       =Gamma |K|.                                   (5)

Thus these caps also keep their exact total budget Q. The total weighted
mass is now

    M_L(t)=|K| sum_p [1+t A(p)]^(-d)>M               (6)

for every small nonzero t and EVERY d>=1, since s^(-d) is strictly convex.
The same fixed slack covers persist in total variation on the original
candidate set. Thus its weighted depth, equivalently the unweighted depth
of the projective image, is strictly below Gamma.

For d=1, (3) would be an equality and cannot establish fixed-base descent;
only the projective assertion is proved here in that dimension. The
single-base case is excluded because no nonconstant A on P exists and
an ordinary simplex really does attain the continuous minimum Gamma.

The calculation is a concrete warning that all first-order moments can
balance while an exact cap-budget-preserving path increases total mass.
No claim is made that arbitrary families admit these affine-radius
or proportional-cap identities.
